skill.name: business-conflict-analyzer
skill.description: Analyzes code changes to identify breaking contracts, schema changes, affected consumers, migration needs, and business impact across supported backend and frontend stacks.
skill.summary: Map code changes to downstream business impact before release or commit.
skill.author: gobeyondyang

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown backticks, test fixtures, locale access, and fixed-argument local commands. Confirmed risks include mutable automatic downloads, Git option injection, out-of-repository scans, persistent hook writes, report overwrites, destructive rollback, and overbroad autonomous-edit instructions. These issues require remediation before unrestricted publication.

remediation.issue: Executable companion files are fetched automatically from a mutable branch.
remediation.suggestion: Pin every fetch URL to an immutable commit and verify a published checksum before loading or execution.

remediation.issue: The --since value can be interpreted as a Git option.
remediation.suggestion: Validate the value with git rev-parse, reject option-like inputs, disable external diff behavior, and separate revisions from paths explicitly.

remediation.issue: Frontend discovery can scan sibling or absolute directories outside the selected repository.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict scans to the repository root by default and require explicit approval for each additional normalized path.

remediation.issue: The Reject workflow uses git checkout -- . and can discard unrelated work.
remediation.suggestion: Show a scoped change preview, preserve unrelated files, create a backup, and require explicit confirmation before any restore command.

remediation.issue: The skill grants itself authority to modify every detected consumer without further confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Present the exact file list and planned edits, then require explicit scope approval before changing files outside the original request.

remediation.issue: Hook installation and report generation modify fixed project paths.
remediation.suggestion: Preview configuration changes, preserve existing hooks, support uninstall automation, and avoid overwriting conflict-report.md without confirmation or versioning.

content.user_title: Analyze Breaking Changes Before You Commit
content.value_statement: Contract and schema changes can break downstream services, clients, and data flows. This skill maps affected references and produces a business impact report before commit.
actual_capabilities: Parses staged, uncommitted, or revision-based Git diffs into structured file and symbol changes.
Classifies changes as P0, P1, or P2 using language-specific contract and schema rules.
Searches backend, frontend, configuration, and historical Git references for affected consumers.
Detects data migration, API versioning, configuration, validation, cache, transaction, and messaging impacts.
Generates English or Chinese Markdown reports with Mermaid dependency graphs and decision options.
Offers an optional Claude Code commit hook that blocks detected P0 changes.
limitations: Results are heuristic and do not replace compilation, tests, schema validation, or service-owner review.
Reference searches cover selected file extensions and may miss generated code, dynamic access, or unsupported languages.
The default frontend scan may inspect sibling directories, and large repositories can increase analysis time.
Remote companion files are fetched from a mutable branch unless the marketplace pins them.

use_cases.title: Review API contract changes
use_cases.description: Trace DTO, endpoint, and response changes to backend clients, frontend consumers, and compatibility requirements.

use_cases.title: Plan database migrations
use_cases.description: Assess DDL changes, existing data risks, service dependencies, and required rollout sequencing.

use_cases.title: Coordinate cross-stack releases
use_cases.description: Produce a shared impact report for services, web clients, tests, and business owners before approval.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze current changes
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of an active working tree
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my current Git changes. List breaking changes, affected consumers, migration needs, and recommended next steps. Do not modify files.

prompt_templates.title: Review a field rename
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the rename of [old field] to [new field] in [contract]. Find backend and frontend consumers. Propose backward-compatible migration steps.

prompt_templates.title: Assess a schema release
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the DDL and API changes since [revision]. Map data, service, message, and client impacts. Produce a phased rollout and rollback plan.

prompt_templates.title: Audit staged changes for commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze staged changes only. Identify P0 and P1 risks, explain evidence, and provide decision options. Do not install hooks or discard changes.

output_examples.input: Rename UserDTO.mobile to phone and assess downstream impact.
output: Risk: High because existing consumers still reference the removed field.
Affected areas: service mappings, frontend profile views, tests, and stored data migration.
Recommendation: retain a compatibility field, update consumers, migrate data, and verify contracts before removal.

output_examples.input: Change the orders endpoint from version one to version two.
output: Risk: Medium when the old route remains available during migration.
Affected areas: API clients, routing tests, documentation, monitoring, and deployment configuration.
Recommendation: add the new route, deprecate the old route, notify owners, and monitor adoption.

output_examples.input: Drop a database column used by an event producer.
output: Risk: High because historical data and message consumers can lose required values.
Required actions: inventory references, backfill or archive data, version the event schema, and coordinate deployment order.

best_practices: Run analysis from the intended repository root and review every external scan path before execution.
Compare findings with compilation, tests, schema checks, and service-owner confirmation before approving changes.
Use pinned skill assets and review the report before applying compatibility fixes or installing the commit guard.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a clean report as proof that unsupported languages, generated code, or dynamic consumers are unaffected.
Do not approve repository-wide automatic fixes without reviewing the complete file list and intended scope.
Do not use broad rollback commands when unrelated working-tree changes may exist.

faq.question: Which languages and frameworks are supported?
faq.answer: It includes rules for Java, Kotlin, Python, TypeScript, JavaScript, Go, Vue, React, JSP, SQL, YAML, XML, and common web frameworks.

faq.question: Does it modify my code?
faq.answer: Analysis scripts generate a report. The skill documentation also proposes optional fixes, rollback actions, and hook installation that require careful approval.

faq.question: Can it block a Git commit?
faq.answer: Yes. The optional Claude Code hook runs the analyzer before git commit and blocks changes classified as P0.

faq.question: Does it replace tests or compilation?
faq.answer: No. It uses heuristics and reference searches. Confirm important findings with builds, tests, contract validation, and owner review.

faq.question: Where is the report saved?
faq.answer: The command-line pipeline writes conflict-report.md in the current project directory and can overwrite an existing file with that name.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: The included scripts are local, but the skill frontmatter automatically fetches companion files from GitHub when loaded.
